extracted.intended_audience: early-career HIV epidemiologists applying for K-type career development awards and grant reviewers/mentors
extracted.subtask_description: A K-01 career development research proposal describing aims, study population, data sources, analytic methods, mentorship/training plan, timeline, and deliverables for evaluating policy effects (ACA/Medicaid expansion) on HIV Care Continuum outcomes using NA-ACCORD and CCASAnet cohort data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aim 1a — Describe disparities in HIVCC outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: To describe disparities in three NHAS-specified HIV Care Continuum outcomes across North America: proportion clinically retained, using ART, or virally suppressed; disparities by demography, geography, patient context (psychiatric diagnosis, regional poverty), and health system characteristics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primarily descriptive analyses highlighting differences across demographic, socioeconomic, psychiatric, geographic, and health system characteristics (e.g., Canada universal ART access vs changing payer structures in US and Mexico).

rubrics_metrics.name: Aim 1b — Temporal trends in HIVCC outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: To describe temporal trends in the three HIVCC outcomes, accounting for geographic, contextual, and health policy differences from 2000 beyond 2014.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use longitudinal data to assess trends over time and how they vary by context and policy; analyses are descriptive and use methods that account for within-individual clustering.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aim 2 — Effect of ACA implementation on HIVCC process outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: To measure the effect of Affordable Care Act (ACA) implementation on HIVCC outcomes (clinical retention, ART use, virologic suppression) using NA-ACCORD clinical cohorts, with comparators including cohorts providing uniform access (e.g., Canadian cohorts) and US states not expanding Medicaid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat Medicaid expansion as a quasi-experimental exposure; use difference-in-differences or piecewise generalized linear mixed models to estimate policy effect modification pre- vs post-ACA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aim 3 — Effect of ACA on clinical endpoints
rubrics_metrics.description: To measure the effect of ACA implementation on HIV disease status at entry and clinical endpoints (CD4+ at enrollment, all-cause mortality, cause-specific mortality) related to competent HIV care in NA-ACCORD.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess non-process outcomes using both interval and clinical cohorts; apply inferential quasi-experimental methods similar to Aim 2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study population inclusion criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Adults contributing geographic data and either laboratory (CD4 count or HIV-1 viral load) or visit data at least once between January 1, 2000 and study close.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Restrict analyses to those with requisite geographic and clinical data; retrospective baseline beginning with available cohort data and continue until at least 2 full years following 2014.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcome: Clinical retention (IOM/NHAS indicator)
rubrics_metrics.description: Retention assigned each year by the IOM/NHAS indicator: ≥2 HIV primary care visits within 12 months, >90 days apart.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assign per-year retention between entry and closing year or year of death; death treated as competing event/absorbent state.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcome: ART use (DHHS indicator)
rubrics_metrics.description: ART use during the year, of those with ≥1 visit in that year, per DHHS indicators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ART defined as multidrug regimens including ≥3 antiretroviral agents; explicitly exclude specified triple-nucleoside regimens (abacavir+tenofovir+lamivudine and didanosine+tenofovir+lamivudine).

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcome: Viral suppression (DHHS indicator)
rubrics_metrics.description: HIV-1 viral load <200 copies/mL at last measurement in the year, of those with ≥1 visit and a measurement in that year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use last available annual measurement to assign suppression status; analyses of viral suppression limited to those with measurements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcome: CD4+ count at enrollment (or at ART start)
rubrics_metrics.description: Defined as the first available CD4+ count within 6 months of enrollment date (or at ART start).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If missing, CD4+ counts may be multiply imputed; missingness will be explored and addressed in sensitivity analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Death handling as competing/absorbent event
rubrics_metrics.description: Death during the study period will be treated as a competing event or 'absorbent state'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Account for death appropriately in longitudinal outcome assignment and inferential models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data sources and comparators
rubrics_metrics.description: Use NA-ACCORD (North America) and CCASAnet (Latin America) cohort data, supplemented with census-derived and publicly-available state/region-level data for contextual variables; use Canadian cohorts and non-expansion states as comparators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leverage breadth and geographic heterogeneity of cohorts; compare expansion vs non-expansion states and universal-access countries for inference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment and linkage of individual and area-level data
rubrics_metrics.description: Align individual-level clinical data with state/region-level data derived from public sources (e.g., census, Kaiser Family Foundation) over time and across countries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rigorous data cleaning, codification, geocoding, and iterative collaboration with data management personnel and bioinformaticians; expect time-consuming preparation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk factor definition and use
rubrics_metrics.description: Include factors such as age, race, sex, injection drug use history, state/jurisdiction of residence, laboratory measures (lipids, HbA1C), diagnoses (psychiatric, hypertension, hyperlipidemia), and clinic encounters as risk factors, mediators, or confounders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat ART regimens, Ryan White eligibility thresholds, and other structural variables as potential confounders/mediators; consider their influence on measured policy effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary descriptive analysis methods (Aim 1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Regression methods using Generalized Estimating Equations (GEE) and restricted cubic splines to assess temporal trends in outcomes, accounting for within-individual clustering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use categorical indicators for health system differences and restricted cubic splines for continuous factors; spatial analyses (regression or cluster detection with likelihood ratio testing) to identify clusters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quasi-experimental inferential methods (Aims 2 and 3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat state Medicaid expansion as a quasi-experimental exposure and use difference-in-differences analysis or piecewise generalized linear mixed models (GLMM) with random intercepts and slopes to assess ACA effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Model specification examples: Yi = β0 + β1Si + β2Ti + β3SiTi for DID; or piecewise GLMM with random effects for intercepts and slopes by state and separate post-ACA intercepts. Consider neighbor-state comparisons to reduce confounding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Random-effects piecewise GLMM specification
rubrics_metrics.description: Logit(πij) = (β0+b0i) + (β00+b00i)*post-ACA + (β1+b1i)*tij*pre-ACA + (β2+b2i)*tij*post-ACA + βx*X with b~N(0,σ2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include random intercepts and slopes by state; interpret β coefficients and random effects for state-level heterogeneity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spatial analysis and cluster detection
rubrics_metrics.description: Use spatial analyses using regression or cluster detection techniques, identifying locations as clusters by likelihood ratio testing (e.g., SaTScan).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detect geographic clustering of outcomes and use mapping/visualization; power for clustering depends on background population, incidence, and spatial distribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Software choices
rubrics_metrics.description: Analyses may be conducted in SaTScan v9.1.1 or R v3.0.3.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use established spatial/statistical packages appropriate to methods chosen.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample size and power considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: With >40,000 patients per year, power to detect an odds ratio of 0.95 or 1.05 for an outcome by an individual factor is >0.90 at α=0.05; detection of a 2% effect in DID requires >10 states and >1 year pre- and post-intervention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For geographic clustering, Tango's statistic (and Kulldorff’s-like statistics) power examples provided; ensure number of events per exposure category sufficient for inference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Missing data handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Explore data missingness (e.g., CD4+ counts at entry) and use multiple imputation techniques if data are missing within sites.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Source data are cleaned and validated, but imputation and sensitivity analyses will be applied where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sensitivity analyses for unmeasured confounding
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct sensitivity analyses for inclusion of unmeasured confounding using Cornfield-type methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess robustness of inferences to unmeasured confounding given multiple influences on receipt of HIV care.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods to improve external validity/transportability
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider inverse probability of selection weighting and develop novel approaches to derive externally valid inferences from cohort data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize translation to a target population is non-trivial; collaborate with Health Policy Methodology and Biostatistics groups to develop/validate methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exploratory modeling: agent-based models
rubrics_metrics.description: Use agent-based modeling to explore plausible effects under different policy decisions and individual behaviors, with parameters derived from observational research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat agent-based models as complementary, 'cutting-edge' techniques to explore policy counterfactuals; involve modeling collaborators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and handling of ART regimens
rubrics_metrics.description: ART will be multidrug regimens including ≥3 antiretroviral agents, excluding specific triple-nucleoside combinations (abacavir+tenofovir+lamivudine and didanosine+tenofovir+lamivudine).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply explicit regimen definitions to classify treatment exposure consistently across cohorts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparator selection to minimize confounding
rubrics_metrics.description: Use cohorts/states with uniform access to care (e.g., Canadian cohorts) and neighboring states with differing expansion status as comparators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Neighboring state comparisons can minimize confounding from regional factors; include Mexican and Canadian populations as universal-access comparators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data management and collaborative infrastructure
rubrics_metrics.description: Rely on a Data Management Core and collaboration with data managers, bioinformaticians, and cohort investigators to clean, validate, geocode, and harmonize multi-cohort data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect semi-annual data transfers from cohorts; timeline accounts for iterative cleaning and potential lags in submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeline and deliverables
rubrics_metrics.description: Detailed multi-year timeline with preparatory tasks (IRB approvals), per-Aim data cleaning/analyses, abstract submissions, internal peer review, manuscript submissions, mapping/visualization hosting, and R01 grant preparation/submission (initial submission Sept. 2019).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deliverables include conference presentations, peer-reviewed manuscripts, data visualizations, and an R01 application; conference attendance limited to ≤9 days/year (2.5% effort).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mentoring and progress monitoring plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Progress monitored via: (1) regular meetings with mentor/co-mentor (≥bi-weekly); (2) ≥semi-annual reviews with mentoring committees; (3) a shared electronic document tracking educational progress, activities, meeting attendance, and progress toward research aims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At outset formulate measurable goals for initial award year: ≥1 oral presentation national/international, ≥3 divisional/center presentations annually, and ≥2 peer-reviewed primary-author publications per year; assessed at regular review meetings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training in Responsible Conduct of Research (RCR)
rubrics_metrics.description: Complete formal RCR training (courses attended at Johns Hopkins and Vanderbilt) and Research Compliance trainings including Human Subjects Research, Conflict of Interest and Commitment, and HIPAA Compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enroll in Vanderbilt's RCR training covering ethics, data management, research fraud, academic misconduct, and conflict of interest; attend seminars/symposia (Ethics Grand Rounds) and relevant coursework (e.g., PUBH 5518 Research Ethics in Health Policy).

rubrics_metrics.name: Measurable career development goals
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific goals to be set with mentors including presentation and publication targets (1 oral presentation; 3 divisional/center presentations annually; 2 primary-author publications per year).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track attainment via shared electronic document and discuss at bi-weekly and semi-annual mentor/committee meetings; mentoring to provide scrutiny and guidance on methods and policy relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation and significance criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: Leverage the vast scope and geographic heterogeneity of NA-ACCORD and CCASAnet to produce uniquely informative evidence on policy impacts on HIVCC outcomes; application of pseudo-experimental design to Medicaid expansion is novel in this context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize novelty of data breadth, cross-country comparisons, and methodological contributions to policy evaluation in HIV epidemiology.
